title: Dual differential line receiver with strobe and on-chip termination

sources.document: National Semiconductor 1975 Interface Integrated Circuits, DS7820/DS8820 dual line receiver

pins.name: IN-1
pins.text: inverting differential input (5 k input resistance typ)

pins.name: TERM1
pins.text: line termination resistor (170 ohm typ) to the non-inverting input; tie to the inverting input to use it

pins.name: RESP1
pins.text: response time control: capacitor to ground slows the receiver to reject noise spikes

pins.name: RESP2
pins.text: response time control: capacitor to ground slows the receiver to reject noise spikes

pins.name: TERM2
pins.text: line termination resistor (170 ohm typ) to the non-inverting input; tie to the inverting input to use it

pins.name: IN-2
pins.text: inverting differential input (5 k input resistance typ)

functions.text: Differential line receiver: the output is high when IN+ is above IN- by more than the threshold (0 V typ, +-0.5 V max with no common mode, +-1 V over +-15 V common mode), low when below. Input range +-15 V. The output state is defined for open inputs (level not read). STROBE gates the output; its polarity and the forced level are not given in the pages read.

electrical.notes: Not a 74-style table: VOL <= 0.4 V at 3.5 mA sink, VOH 2.5..5.5 V at 0.2 mA source (fanout of two TTL). VCC 4.75..5.25 V for DS8820.

unknown: STROBE polarity and the output level it forces are not stated in the pages read (only strobe current: 1.0/1.4 mA at 0.4 V).
Output level for open inputs not stated in the pages read.
Output stage type: the schematic shows an emitter-follower pull-up with resistor and a transistor pull-down; recorded as totem-pole.
The ND manual calls this part "Tri-state line receiver"; the DS8820 has no three-state output. The ND pinout (1 -, 2 terminate, 3 +, 4 strobe, 6 output) matches the DS8820 exactly.
Only a typical response time is printed; no tPLH/tPHL split and no maximum.
notes: Two independent receivers. ND symbol shows one half with pin numbers of the other half in brackets.
